pageCache.pageTitle: Gidea Park Primary School - Vision & Values
pageCache.text:
Vision & Values
Achieving Excellence Together
We want our learners to be aspirational, to set themselves challenging goals and to work hard, growing in confidence and acquiring the skills needed to succeed in these aims.
Working together in partnership, we can support our learners in achieving their goals. We aim to instill in our learners the belief that learning is limitless, that the world is full of opportunities waiting to be grasped and that through effort and perseverance everyone can achieve.
Our Core Values
Our vision is underpinned by our core values of perseverance, independence, respect, achievement and responsibility which are central to all that we do. These were devised in consultation with the whole school community and reflect our collaborative approach to everything here at Gidea Park Primary. Through these values we seek to develop rounded learners who are able to make a positive contribution to society.
We show perseverance by making sure we keep going when at first things seem difficult
We show independence by listening and learning until we are ready to try by ourselves
We show respect by being considerate and thoughtful towards all staff and pupils in the school
We achieve by trying to produce work to the highest standard of which we are capable
We take responsibility for our own choices and actions

pageCache.pageTitle: Gidea Park Primary School - Headteacher's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to our school website!
Everything that we do at Gidea Park Primary centres around our school motto, ‘Achieving Excellence Together’. Our school is a successful, vibrant school; a school where children come first. Our children are enthusiastic and motivated to seize endless opportunities. We strive to ensure that our children are provided with learning opportunities that are relevant now and in the future.
At Gidea Park, we believe that children should be curious about learning and see themselves as lifelong learners. Through our engaging curriculum, we ensure that pupils can foster a passion for learning that develops high aspirations and a lifetime of memories. We want our pupils to develop into empathetic, respectful and responsible members of society.
The school has a dedicated team that works hard to reach high standards in everything that we do. We firmly believe that education is a partnership between home and school and regard you as an active partner in your child’s education. Together we can help your child achieve excellence in all that they do.

Breakfast & After School Club
Breakfast and After School clubs at the school are run by First Class Kids, a well-established organisation with a strong reputation for delivering high-quality childcare services.
Their experienced and dedicated team is committed to creating a safe, nurturing, and engaging environment for all children. They offer a range of activities designed to support the educational and social development of students, including:
Breakfast Club provision runs from 7.30am to 8.40am at a cost of £5.50 per child per session.
After School Club provision runs from 3.15pm to 6.00pm at a cost of £17.00 per child per session.
Please note this provision is run independently of the school and any queries should be directed to First Class Kids. For more information, please see the links below to visit their website or download their handbook and booking form. Alternatively, owner and director Kelly Clancy can be contacted by phone on 07597366551 or by email at firstclasskidsclub@hotmail.com.

Maths
Maths at Gidea Park
At Gidea Park we are working with our local Maths Hub to be a 'teaching for mastery' school. This approach aims to build understanding and enjoyment of maths in all pupils, building their ability to reason and make connections in their thinking. For more information you can visit the website of the National Centre for Excellence in the Teaching of Mathematics (NCETM).
Curriculum
The school follows the structure of the NCETM Curriculum Prioritisation, using this as a basis to develop rigorous, challenging lessons that are well-tailored to the needs of our pupils. The school uses materials from NCETM and a range of other sources to develop a bespoke and ever-changing curriculum matched closely to the ever-changing needs of our learners.
Number Facts
Essential number facts such as number bonds and times tables are taught throughout the school as needed. Programmes Numbots and Times Tables Rockstars are used at school and at home to facilitate practice, and pupils work towards Times Tables Badges in school to mark their progress and achievement.
Parental Support
One of the most important things parents can do is encourage. Maths can hold a stigma for some, and parents often claim they 'didn't get' maths or just are 'not good at it'. We want to encourage all our pupils that maths is for them and build a positive, resilient, can-do attitude. In terms of specifics, regular practice of number bonds and times tables is of huge benefit throughout children's time at school. As children progress through KS2, they will also be given an increasing amount of maths homework, so creating a routine and expectation around this is essential.

Reading Badges
Each year, children are challenged to earn their Reading Badge by reading 20 books over the course of the year. Each book needs to be filled in on the relevant page in children's Home School Diaries, and signed off by a parent/carer at home or teacher at school.
Challenge
In an attempt to broaden children's reading experiences, the challenge involves reading 10 books of children's own choice and 10 from a recommended reading list. Lists can be found below and will open up in a new window; they are sourced from the website School Reading List, which also gives you a summary of each book, along with full reviews for some, if you need help making a selection. The website also contains a host of other information and recommendations for parents, including poetry, graphic novels, picture books, bedtime reading for adults to read to their children, and more.
Each year a different coloured badge is available - can you collect the whole set of seven over your time at Gidea Park?

Reading
Reading at Gidea Park
At Gidea Park we believe that learning to read is one of the most important things your child will achieve at our school. A positive first experience of reading can shape a child’s love of books and help develop every aspect of their learning, so we put great effort into making every child a reader as quickly as possible. Throughout their time at Gidea Park, children are exposed to a wide range of diverse and engaging texts through shared, guided and independent reading giving them solid foundations for starting secondary schools.
Reading for Pleasure
We firmly believe that Reading for Pleasure is as important as learning good reading strategies, so we work hard to maintain our class libraries, regularly renewing and updating our texts. We had two very successful book fairs which enabled us to purchase new books for each class. We try to be creative in our range of reading materials and, with the development of our curriculum, are extending the range of non-fiction texts to help the children make meaningful connections within our topics.
Key Stage One have a daily DEAR (Drop Everything And Read) time, where children may read to themselves or an adult might share a book with the class. Key Stage Two have one weekly reading lesson designated for Reading for Pleasure, giving opportunities both for children to read and for teachers to promote a love of reading.
What Reading Looks Like at Gidea Park
Each year group has specific authors they focus on so the children become familiar with the author’s style and, as they move up through the school, can make comparisons between texts and authors. This also gives them an informed choice over their likes and dislikes.
Vocabulary development is something we prioritise – we introduce new vocabulary frequently, which we encourage the children to use in context. We also have vocabulary lists which we cover as part of our topic work.
Children practise reading books that match the phonics phase they are learning. We use the Read Write Inc scheme for this, and children will take a book from this scheme home with them to share with parents.
Children continue to work through the phonics scheme and read the linked book. Once children have graduated from the RWI Phonics scheme, normally in Year 2, showing they can both decode and read at speed, focus shifts more heavily onto comprehension; at this stage children become 'free readers' and are invited to take appropriate books of their choice home from the class library.
Each year group has core texts which have been thoughtfully selected to ensure the children are exposed to a broad range of genres and different language structures. The key comprehension skills we aim to embed are:
Children will take a copy of their core text home and will be given a number of pages or chapters to read for the following week.
Explanation – describing in detail
Sequencing – ordering parts of the text
Tracking and Progress
Class teachers assess the children’s reading skills regularly so that we can ensure they are making good progress in both decoding words and understanding the text. Children who are exceeding the targets are encouraged to choose challenging and diverse reading material. Any children who are not making the expected progress will be given additional support.
Parental Support
As part of our home / school agreement our pupils are expected to read regularly at home with parental support. The children are encouraged to achieve their reading badge, which they receive when they have read twenty age-appropriate books at home. This is then celebrated in class; see our Reading Badge page for more detail.
Recommended Reads
To find a comprehensive list of books suitable for each year group go to:
www.booksfortopics.com
and go to the tab ‘Key Stage Book Lists’.
This website also provides book suggestions for a range of different topics.
Reading Badge
See our Reading Badge page for more detail on how your child can earn their reading badge.
